The Cut — three things the system never does
1. Never emails a real prospect. to: is hardcoded to one
inbox, and the Growth Lead clicks before anything sends.
2. Never scores a claim whose quote does not support it.
R-23 drops it to asserted — it still shows, at zero.
3. Never guesses past the cap. Four extra fetches, then a
named handoff — "try harder" is not an available answer.
Checks 07 and 08 of the Nine both landed in Boundary. This is
where the human was put, and it is what made the build buildable.
Gemini Flash (gemini-3.8-flash, pinned as a const — a runtime
guard throws if a non-Gemini id is ever resolved) reads prose
in five places: extract, next-page choice, pain points, draft,
reply intent. Every verdict, score, gate, tier, ladder rank,
completeness check and reply action is plain TypeScript.
The loop's stopping condition is the clearest case: a model
asked "do you know enough?" will say yes about a blank page,
so code counts the empty fields instead. Same input, same
verdict — asserted by a test, not by a claim.
cost_ledger holds a row per AI call. Across 5 runs: $0.2685
(≈ ₹22.55) over 347 calls, of which 194 were cache hits.
Hunter: 8 credits used of 50, billed per email returned.
AI_COST_CEILING_USD stops a run cleanly and keeps the rows
already finished. Vercel Hobby and Neon free tier are $0.
